events.title: The Battle of Trafalgar
events.description: Off the coast of Spain, a British fleet under Admiral Horatio Nelson defeated the combined French and Spanish fleets. Nelson was mortally wounded by a sniper during the battle, but he lived long enough to learn that victory was assured.
events.significance: The victory confirmed British naval supremacy for roughly a century. It ended Napoleon's hopes of invading Britain by sea.

events.title: Edison Demonstrates His Electric Lamp
events.description: After about fourteen months of testing, Thomas Edison showed that his incandescent electric lamp worked. He hoped it would one day compete with gas lighting.
events.significance: The lamp was a key step toward practical electric lighting. It helped change how homes, businesses and cities were lit.

events.title: Subhas Chandra Bose Proclaims a Provisional Government of Free India
events.description: At a mass rally in Singapore, the exiled nationalist leader Subhas Chandra Bose declared the creation of Azad Hind, or Free India. He was named its Head of State, Prime Minister and Minister for War.
events.significance: The proclamation was a bold, controversial challenge to British rule during World War II. It remains an important chapter in the story of India's independence movement.

events.title: The Guggenheim Museum Opens in New York
events.description: The Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum opened its Frank Lloyd Wright-designed building on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan. Its spiraling white rotunda was a radical departure from traditional museum architecture.
events.significance: The building became one of the 20th century's most celebrated architectural landmarks. It also reshaped how museums present art.
